You are acting as an expert software engineer and research assistant tasked with executing the Phase 4 gate for the OsBiruBob project at [https://github.com/HeitorM50/OsBiruBob](https://github.com/HeitorM50/OsBiruBob). This prompt provides an exhaustive, end-to-end specification for executing, verifying, and documenting this validation gate.

The purpose of the Phase 4 gate is to empirically verify inside the Bob IDE that the configuration artifacts and optimization prescriptions generated by Hindsight during Phase 4 are successfully accepted, loaded, and reflected in the telemetry export of a subsequent session. This gate serves as a strict structural checkpoint proving that configuration changes have been applied correctly to the environment. It does not aim to prove the final economic savings or comprehensive behavioral shifts, both of which are strictly reserved for the full execution and evaluation in Round B and Phase 5.

This gate directly integrates the deliverables of two prerequisite issues: Issue 16, which generates a deterministic, safe AGENTS.md file from diagnostic findings, and Issue 17, which produces prescriptions for disabling unneeded tools and reviewing skill overhead.

Before launching any validation session in Bob IDE, you must conduct a rigorous pre-condition audit. First, inspect the proposed AGENTS.md artifact to confirm that it is concise, targeted, and fully compliant with the project redaction policy. The file must contain zero sensitive evidence, zero private conversation transcripts, zero tool call arguments, zero raw prompt text, and zero absolute system paths or personal directory names. Second, compile an explicit decision log specifying all prescriptions to be enacted. This log must categorize all tools into three clear groups: non-essential tools approved for disabling, essential tools that must remain enabled for ongoing development, and idle tools that were deliberately retained because they provide essential fallback capabilities. Third, if any manual modifications are made to skill configurations, record the exact toggles applied while documenting the foundational domain constraint that the Round A baseline export only provided an aggregate 1,541 tokens for skills and never attributed that overhead to any individual named skill. Fourth, ensure all Round A baseline datasets, including benchmark/rodada-a.json and associated session summaries, are safely archived for comparative analysis.

Next, execute the validation procedure within Bob IDE following these precise steps. Place the reviewed AGENTS.md file in the root directory of the repository being used for validation. In the Bob IDE settings or mode configuration, apply the tool disabling prescriptions by disabling exclusively the approved non-essential tools and verifying that every essential tool remains active. If a skill configuration adjustment is part of the test plan, apply the exact change and record the before and after state. Start a new, short validation session in Bob IDE. In this session, execute a minimal, non-destructive, and lightweight task such as reading the project README or checking repository status, ensuring the task can be completed entirely with the retained toolset without triggering tool missing errors or execution failures. Keep the session strictly focused and brief to avoid depleting the operational token budget reserved for Round B. Once the task finishes, export the raw session JSON from Bob IDE and capture a full summary screenshot. Save the screenshot directly inside the bob_sessions/ directory using the standardized project naming pattern.

Once the session export is obtained, pass the raw JSON content into the pure Observe pipeline to generate the corresponding ObserveReport. Evaluate the resulting metrics against the following mandatory validation rules.

First, inspect breakdown.projectRules in the ObserveReport. This value must be strictly greater than zero, which serves as definitive proof that Bob IDE recognized, parsed, and injected the AGENTS.md rules into the agent context window. You must not attempt to derive or assert an exact mathematical conversion between the byte size of AGENTS.md and the reported projectRules token count, as the export format does not define a predictable byte-to-token ratio.

Second, examine the availableTools array in the ObserveReport. The array must match the intended tool configuration exactly. Every tool that was prescribed for disabling and approved must be completely absent from availableTools. Every tool designated as essential must remain present in availableTools. Ensure that no uncataloged or unknown tools were silently dropped from the telemetry or decision logs without explicit documentation.

Third, analyze the breakdown.toolDefinitions metric. If tools were successfully disabled, the total tool definition tokens in the new export should show a downward trend compared to the 5,403 tokens observed in the baseline. However, you must not attribute any specific token difference to a single tool, because the telemetry export only provides an aggregate sum across all active tool schemas.

Fourth, inspect breakdown.skills only if manual adjustments were made to skill configurations during the pre-condition phase. If skill configurations were modified, record the new token count and compare it against the baseline 1,541 tokens. If skill configurations were left untouched, do not draw conclusions from this field. Under no circumstances should you invent or assert that a specific named skill was the root cause of the baseline skill overhead.

Fifth, verify task completion integrity by checking that tasks[0].completed is true and is derived strictly from stop equals true in the raw export. This confirms that the reduced toolset and new project rules allowed the session to terminate naturally and successfully without being blocked by missing capabilities.

Sixth, acknowledge that the absence of observable behavioral changes in this short validation session does not invalidate the success of the gate. Behavioral adaptation and instruction adherence will be evaluated across the longer, multi-step workflows of Round B.

Prior to closing the gate and before commencing Round B, you must formulate and formally record the mandatory Round B hypothesis. This hypothesis must detail the expected directional movement of all key metrics, specifically: an expected reduction in fixedOverhead, an expected reduction in toolDefinitions if tools were removed, an expected value of projectRules strictly greater than zero, an expected change in skills only if skill toggles were applied, the exact inventory expected in availableTools, an assessment of potential operational side effects or risks, and a clear distinction identifying which metrics represent empirical measurements and which represent estimated projections. An acceptable hypothesis statement should follow this pattern: With the reviewed AGENTS.md active and non-essential tools disabled, we project projectRules greater than zero, a reduction in toolDefinitions below 5,403 tokens, and an overall decrease in fixedOverhead from the baseline 10,439 tokens, with the exact numerical savings recognized as an estimate that will be measured empirically during Round B.

Compile all validation results into a comprehensive evidence artifact. This artifact must include: the exact commit hash or configuration version tested; the full redacted text or clean unified diff of the applied AGENTS.md; the complete tool classification tables listing prescribed tools, actually disabled tools, and retained essential tools; documentation of any manual skill changes; the key metrics extracted from the new ObserveReport including breakdown.projectRules, breakdown.toolDefinitions, breakdown.skills, fixedOverhead, availableTools, loadedSkills, and task completion via stop equals true; the file path of the summary screenshot in bob_sessions/; a safe before-and-after metric comparison table comparing baseline values against validation values; and the finalized Round B hypothesis statement.

Confirm that all out-of-scope boundaries are strictly respected: do not attempt to prove the final economic impact, do not assign individual token costs to specific tools or skills, do not demand deep behavioral shifts during the validation turn, do not execute or analyze Round B tasks within this issue, and do not attempt to write code that automates internal Bob IDE configuration mechanisms.

Complete the audit, verify that all acceptance criteria are met, ensure all published data is fully redacted according to project guidelines, and record the execution evidence to finalize the Phase 4 gate.

# Project Instructions (AGENTS.md)

# AGENTS.md — Hindsight

Context for AI coding assistants. Keep this file short and stable.

---

## What this project is

A **static web app** (plus a dev CLI) that analyses IBM Bob session exports,
identifies context waste, generates corrected configuration — `AGENTS.md`, tools to
disable, Skills, MCPs, subagents — and compares two experiment rounds (A/B).

Pipeline: `export JSON → Parser → Observe → Diagnose → Prescribe → Compare → UI`

Everything runs **in the browser**. No backend, no database, no network calls, no
API key. A session export contains source code, absolute paths, and the commands the
user ran — it must never leave the machine. This is a hard constraint, not a
preference.

`ObserveReport` is the central contract: after F2, **no module reads the raw export**.

---

## Repository map

```
benchmark/          experiment protocol, task prompt, and both round exports
  METRICS.md        what is measured and the rules that make the comparison valid
  rodada-a.json     Round A — baseline (same as fixtures/sample-export.json)
  rodada-b.json     Round B — with generated config
  task.txt          exact benchmark prompt (character-for-character)
bob_sessions/       required screenshots of Bob sessions (submission deliverable)
docs/
  architecture.md   component responsibilities, data flow, dependency rules
  domain-model.md   all domain types with invariants (source of truth for types)
  technology-stack.md  stack decisions, commands, and justifications
  schema.md         Bob export JSON structure, field-by-field
  analise-rodada-a.md  findings from the baseline run
  ROADMAP.md        phases F0–F7, gates, and Bobcoin strategy
fixtures/
  sample-export.json  faithful copy of rodada-a.json — use for all dev/tests
data/               curated catalogues — versioned data, not code
  mcp-catalog.json    binary → MCP server (drives enable-mcp)
  tool-catalog.json   tool → purpose → group (groups unused-tool findings)
src/
  domain/types.ts   TypeScript interfaces for all domain types
  parser/           F2: validates and normalises the raw export → Session
  observe/          F2: extracts metrics from Session → ObserveReport
  diagnose/         F3: pure detectors (ObserveReport) → Finding[]
  prescribe/        F4: generates config artifacts from Finding[] + catalogues
  compare/          F5: diffs two ObserveReports → Comparison
  ui/               F6: the React SPA — this is the product
  cli.ts            F6: same core, terminal output — dev tool only
```

---

## Canonical commands

All commands run from the repository root.

```bash
npm ci                # install — use npm install only when adding a dependency
npm test              # run tests (vitest run)
npm run test:watch    # watch mode during development
npm run typecheck     # tsc --noEmit — run before every commit
npm run dev:web       # vite — the SPA with hot reload (this is the product)
npm run build:web     # vite build → dist/web/ (static, deployable)
npm run preview       # vite preview — check the static build locally
npm run dev           # tsx src/cli.ts — CLI without building
npm run build         # tsup → dist/cli.js
npm run demo          # build + run the CLI over fixtures/sample-export.json
```

---

## Code and test conventions

- **TypeScript strict mode.** `strict: true` in tsconfig.json. No `any`.
- **One module per pipeline stage.** `parser → observe → diagnose → prescribe → compare → cli`.
  Dependencies flow downward only — see `docs/architecture.md` for the
  full prohibition list.
- **Test files alongside source.** Pattern: `src/**/*.test.ts` and `src/**/*.test.tsx`.
  Fixtures go in `fixtures/`; tests import from there.
- **Pure functions for detectors.** Each detector in `src/diagnose/` is
  `(ObserveReport) => Finding[]` with no side effects.
- **No rounding in domain.** `Math.round`, `toFixed`, and truncation are
  forbidden in `src/domain/`, `src/parser/`, `src/observe/`, `src/diagnose/`,
  `src/prescribe/`, and `src/compare/`. Round only in `src/cli.ts`.
- **Timestamps are epoch milliseconds.** Type `EpochMs = number`. Never
  convert to `Date` or ISO string before the presentation layer.
- **Subtasks excluded from aggregation.** `task.parentId !== null` = subtask.
  Never add its cost/tokens to session totals (invariant I-5).
- **The core must stay browser-safe.** No Node APIs (`fs`, `path`, `process`, `os`)
  anywhere except `src/cli.ts`. The web build imports the same modules.
- **No network, ever.** No `fetch`, `XMLHttpRequest`, WebSocket, telemetry — in any
  module, including the UI. The bundle is self-contained.
- **No LLM calls.** Recommendations are rule + catalogue, deterministic and traceable
  to a field in the export. Calling a model would break demo-without-API-key, static
  deploy, privacy, and explainability at once. See `docs/architecture.md`.
- **Never render export content as HTML.** No `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, `innerHTML`
  or `eval`. The export is untrusted input in the browser too.
- **Absence is not zero.** A metric the export does not provide goes into
  `unavailableMetrics` or stays `null` — never `0`. Estimates must be labelled as
  estimates (invariant I-6).

---

## Confirmed schema traps (read before touching parser or tests)

These bugs have been confirmed on the real export — do not re-discover them:

| Trap | Correct behaviour |
|---|---|
| `messages[].createdAt` is identical for all messages | Order by `data._meta.timestamp` |
| `_meta.spend` only exists on `assistant` messages | Guard the access — accessing it on `tool` or `user` crashes |
| One `assistant` turn can have N parallel `toolCalls[]` | Correlate by `.id`, never by position |
| `task.status` stays `"active"` after completion | Use `stop: true` on the last assistant message |
| `contextWindowBreakdown.total` ≠ `reportedTotal` | Intentional: `total` = fixed overhead, `reportedTotal` = overhead + conversation |
| `gitSha` and `gitBranch` are always `null` | Record commit SHA manually via screenshot |
| `tasks[].task.parentId !== null` = subtask | Do not double-count it in session aggregates |
| `_meta.spend` is `undefined`, not `null`, when absent | Use optional chaining: `msg.data._meta.spend?.cost` |

---

## Policy: sensitive data

**Never print, log, or copy into a generated artefact:**
- `data.content` of user or assistant messages
- `toolCalls[].arguments` (may contain file paths, commands, or code)
- `toolUsage.signature.arguments`
- `task.title` (it is the full prompt, often verbatim code)
- `task.env.staticEnvInfo.primaryWorkspace` (absolute path)

These fields are available internally for analysis but must be redacted
(`[REDACTED]`) before any output visible to the user, unless the user
explicitly enables raw display.

The `evidence.redactable` flag on a `Finding` marks which evidence fields
need redaction. Check it before rendering.

Catalogues in `data/` are the exception: they are **trusted input** (versioned and
reviewed in PR), so their text may be rendered directly.

---

## Where to implement each phase

| Phase | Files to create/modify | Input type | Output type |
|---|---|---|---|
| **F2 — Observe** | `src/parser/`, `src/observe/` | raw JSON bytes | `Session`, `ObserveReport` |
| **F3 — Diagnose** | `src/diagnose/` | `ObserveReport` | `Finding[]` |
| **F4 — Prescribe** | `src/prescribe/` | `Finding[]` | `Prescription[]`, `AGENTS.md` draft |
| **F5 — Verify** | `src/compare/` | two `ObserveReport`s | `Comparison` |
| **F6 — Interface** | `src/ui/` (product), `src/cli.ts` (dev) | all of the above | four screens / terminal output |

Each module has its own test file(s). The fixture for all tests is
`fixtures/sample-export.json` (copy of the real Round A baseline).

---

## Definition of Done (per issue)

A task is done only when:
- acceptance criteria are covered by a test or recorded evidence
- `npm test` passes
- `npm run typecheck` passes
- invalid input fails with a readable message
- no secret or private content appears in output
- the result has been verified against `benchmark/rodada-a.json` when applicable

</project_rules>

## Purpose
This tool exists for exactly one job, and it is a narrow one: producing a static overview or summary of a larger, already-completed body of work, packaged as a shareable one-pager. Good examples of what belongs here: a finished report summarizing findings, a wrap-up of a multi-step task the user just finished with you, a consolidated view of results gathered across a conversation, or a polished recap someone could forward to a colleague without further editing. This is not a general-purpose "make it look nicer" formatter, and it is not a way to make any output feel more finished — most of what you produce in a conversation, including long or well-organized answers, should still just be a normal chat reply. 1. Only for an overview or summary of a completed body of work. If the content you're about to generate is itself the primary deliverable — a single answer to a question, one example, one explanation — it does not qualify, even if it's long, even if it's detailed, and even if formatting it as a page would look good. 2. Static content only, with no exceptions. <script> tags and all inline event handlers are stripped automatically when the artifact is saved, so nothing you produce through this tool can ever actually be interactive, no matter how it's written — buttons won't click, forms won't submit, calculators won't calculate. 3. Never a substitute for a code snippet or a mermaid diagram, even when the underlying content happens to be HTML or CSS. This artifact must include: the exact commit hash or configuration version tested; the full redacted text or clean unified diff of the applied AGENTS.md; the complete tool classification tables listing prescribed tools, actually disabled tools, and retained essential tools; documentation of any manual skill changes; the key metrics extracted from the new ObserveReport including breakdown.projectRules, breakdown.toolDefinitions, breakdown.skills, fixedOverhead, availableTools, loadedSkills, and task completion via stop equals true; the file path of the summary screenshot in bob_sessions/; a safe before-and-after metric comparison table comparing baseline values against validation values; and the finalized Round B hypothesis statement.

Confirm that all out-of-scope boundaries are strictly respected: do not attempt to prove the final economic impact, do not assign individual token costs to specific tools or skills, do not demand deep behavioral shifts during the validation turn, do not execute or analyze Round B tasks within this issue, and do not attempt to write code that automates internal Bob IDE configuration mechanisms.

1 | # AGENTS.md — Hindsight
2 | 
3 | Context for AI coding assistants. Keep this file short and stable.
4 | 
5 | ---
6 | 
7 | ## What this project is
8 | 
9 | A **static web app** (plus a dev CLI) that analyses IBM Bob session exports,
10 | identifies context waste, generates corrected configuration — `AGENTS.md`, tools to
11 | disable, Skills, MCPs, subagents — and compares two experiment rounds (A/B).
12 | 
13 | Pipeline: `export JSON → Parser → Observe → Diagnose → Prescribe → Compare → UI`
14 | 
15 | Everything runs **in the browser**. No backend, no database, no network calls, no
16 | API key. A session export contains source code, absolute paths, and the commands the
17 | user ran — it must never leave the machine. This is a hard constraint, not a
18 | preference.
19 | 
20 | `ObserveReport` is the central contract: after F2, **no module reads the raw export**.
21 | 
22 | ---
23 | 
24 | ## Repository map
25 | 
26 | ```
27 | benchmark/          experiment protocol, task prompt, and both round exports
28 |   METRICS.md        what is measured and the rules that make the comparison valid
29 |   rodada-a.json     Round A — baseline (same as fixtures/sample-export.json)
30 |   rodada-b.json     Round B — with generated config
31 |   task.txt          exact benchmark prompt (character-for-character)
32 | bob_sessions/       required screenshots of Bob sessions (submission deliverable)
33 | docs/
34 |   architecture.md   component responsibilities, data flow, dependency rules
35 |   domain-model.md   all domain types with invariants (source of truth for types)
36 |   technology-stack.md  stack decisions, commands, and justifications
37 |   schema.md         Bob export JSON structure, field-by-field
38 |   analise-rodada-a.md  findings from the baseline run
39 |   ROADMAP.md        phases F0–F7, gates, and Bobcoin strategy
40 | fixtures/
41 |   sample-export.json  faithful copy of rodada-a.json — use for all dev/tests
42 | data/               curated catalogues — versioned data, not code
43 |   mcp-catalog.json    binary → MCP server (drives enable-mcp)
44 |   tool-catalog.json   tool → purpose → group (groups unused-tool findings)
45 | src/
46 |   domain/types.ts   TypeScript interfaces for all domain types
47 |   parser/           F2: validates and normalises the raw export → Session
48 |   observe/          F2: extracts metrics from Session → ObserveReport
49 |   diagnose/         F3: pure detectors (ObserveReport) → Finding[]
50 |   prescribe/        F4: generates config artifacts from Finding[] + catalogues
51 |   compare/          F5: diffs two ObserveReports → Comparison
52 |   ui/               F6: the React SPA — this is the product
53 |   cli.ts            F6: same core, terminal output — dev tool only
54 | ```
55 | 
56 | ---
57 | 
58 | ## Canonical commands
59 | 
60 | All commands run from the repository root.
61 | 
62 | ```bash
63 | npm ci                # install — use npm install only when adding a dependency
64 | npm test              # run tests (vitest run)
65 | npm run test:watch    # watch mode during development
66 | npm run typecheck     # tsc --noEmit — run before every commit
67 | npm run dev:web       # vite — the SPA with hot reload (this is the product)
68 | npm run build:web     # vite build → dist/web/ (static, deployable)
69 | npm run preview       # vite preview — check the static build locally
70 | npm run dev           # tsx src/cli.ts — CLI without building
71 | npm run build         # tsup → dist/cli.js
72 | npm run demo          # build + run the CLI over fixtures/sample-export.json
73 | ```
74 | 
75 | ---
76 | 
77 | ## Code and test conventions
78 | 
79 | - **TypeScript strict mode.** `strict: true` in tsconfig.json. No `any`.
80 | - **One module per pipeline stage.** `parser → observe → diagnose → prescribe → compare → cli`.
81 |   Dependencies flow downward only — see `docs/architecture.md` for the
82 |   full prohibition list.
83 | - **Test files alongside source.** Pattern: `src/**/*.test.ts` and `src/**/*.test.tsx`.
84 |   Fixtures go in `fixtures/`; tests import from there.
85 | - **Pure functions for detectors.** Each detector in `src/diagnose/` is
86 |   `(ObserveReport) => Finding[]` with no side effects.
87 | - **No rounding in domain.** `Math.round`, `toFixed`, and truncation are
88 |   forbidden in `src/domain/`, `src/parser/`, `src/observe/`, `src/diagnose/`,
89 |   `src/prescribe/`, and `src/compare/`. Round only in `src/cli.ts`.
90 | - **Timestamps are epoch milliseconds.** Type `EpochMs = number`. Never
91 |   convert to `Date` or ISO string before the presentation layer.
92 | - **Subtasks excluded from aggregation.** `task.parentId !== null` = subtask.
93 |   Never add its cost/tokens to session totals (invariant I-5).
94 | - **The core must stay browser-safe.** No Node APIs (`fs`, `path`, `process`, `os`)
95 |   anywhere except `src/cli.ts`. The web build imports the same modules.
96 | - **No network, ever.** No `fetch`, `XMLHttpRequest`, WebSocket, telemetry — in any
97 |   module, including the UI. The bundle is self-contained.
98 | - **No LLM calls.** Recommendations are rule + catalogue, deterministic and traceable
99 |   to a field in the export. Calling a model would break demo-without-API-key, static
100 |   deploy, privacy, and explainability at once. See `docs/architecture.md`.
101 | - **Never render export content as HTML.** No `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, `innerHTML`
102 |   or `eval`. The export is untrusted input in the browser too.
103 | - **Absence is not zero.** A metric the export does not provide goes into
104 |   `unavailableMetrics` or stays `null` — never `0`. Estimates must be labelled as
105 |   estimates (invariant I-6).
106 | 
107 | ---
108 | 
109 | ## Confirmed schema traps (read before touching parser or tests)
110 | 
111 | These bugs have been confirmed on the real export — do not re-discover them:
112 | 
113 | | Trap | Correct behaviour |
114 | |---|---|
115 | | `messages[].createdAt` is identical for all messages | Order by `data._meta.timestamp` |
116 | | `_meta.spend` only exists on `assistant` messages | Guard the access — accessing it on `tool` or `user` crashes |
117 | | One `assistant` turn can have N parallel `toolCalls[]` | Correlate by `.id`, never by position |
118 | | `task.status` stays `"active"` after completion | Use `stop: true` on the last assistant message |
119 | | `contextWindowBreakdown.total` ≠ `reportedTotal` | Intentional: `total` = fixed overhead, `reportedTotal` = overhead + conversation |
120 | | `gitSha` and `gitBranch` are always `null` | Record commit SHA manually via screenshot |
121 | | `tasks[].task.parentId !== null` = subtask | Do not double-count it in session aggregates |
122 | | `_meta.spend` is `undefined`, not `null`, when absent | Use optional chaining: `msg.data._meta.spend?.cost` |
123 | 
124 | ---
125 | 
126 | ## Policy: sensitive data
127 | 
128 | **Never print, log, or copy into a generated artefact:**
129 | - `data.content` of user or assistant messages
130 | - `toolCalls[].arguments` (may contain file paths, commands, or code)
131 | - `toolUsage.signature.arguments`
132 | - `task.title` (it is the full prompt, often verbatim code)
133 | - `task.env.staticEnvInfo.primaryWorkspace` (absolute path)
134 | 
135 | These fields are available internally for analysis but must be redacted
136 | (`[REDACTED]`) before any output visible to the user, unless the user
137 | explicitly enables raw display.
138 | 
139 | The `evidence.redactable` flag on a `Finding` marks which evidence fields
140 | need redaction. Check it before rendering.
141 | 
142 | Catalogues in `data/` are the exception: they are **trusted input** (versioned and
143 | reviewed in PR), so their text may be rendered directly.
144 | 
145 | ---
146 | 
147 | ## Where to implement each phase
148 | 
149 | | Phase | Files to create/modify | Input type | Output type |
150 | |---|---|---|---|
151 | | **F2 — Observe** | `src/parser/`, `src/observe/` | raw JSON bytes | `Session`, `ObserveReport` |
152 | | **F3 — Diagnose** | `src/diagnose/` | `ObserveReport` | `Finding[]` |
153 | | **F4 — Prescribe** | `src/prescribe/` | `Finding[]` | `Prescription[]`, `AGENTS.md` draft |
154 | | **F5 — Verify** | `src/compare/` | two `ObserveReport`s | `Comparison` |
155 | | **F6 — Interface** | `src/ui/` (product), `src/cli.ts` (dev) | all of the above | four screens / terminal output |
156 | 
157 | Each module has its own test file(s). The fixture for all tests is
158 | `fixtures/sample-export.json` (copy of the real Round A baseline).
159 | 
160 | ---
161 | 
162 | ## Definition of Done (per issue)
163 | 
164 | A task is done only when:
165 | - acceptance criteria are covered by a test or recorded evidence
166 | - `npm test` passes
167 | - `npm run typecheck` passes
168 | - invalid input fails with a readable message
169 | - no secret or private content appears in output
170 | - the result has been verified against `benchmark/rodada-a.json` when applicable
171 |

1 | # Análise da Rodada A (baseline)
2 | 
3 | Leitura de [`benchmark/rodada-a.json`](../benchmark/rodada-a.json), o export real do
4 | baseline. Escrita antes de qualquer detector existir, direto do arquivo.
5 | 
6 | ---
7 | 
8 | ## Números
9 | 
10 | | Métrica | Valor |
11 | |---|---|
12 | | Custo total | **US$ 0,336902** |
13 | | Contexto final (`reportedTotal`) | **17.584 tokens** |
14 | | Overhead fixo (`breakdown.total`) | **10.439 tokens** |
15 | | Conversa (`reportedTotal − total`) | 7.145 tokens |
16 | | Mensagens | 21 — 1 `system`, 1 `user`, 5 `assistant`, 14 `tool` |
17 | | Turnos do assistente | **5** |
18 | | Chamadas de ferramenta | **14** |
19 | | Chamadas com erro (`isError: true`) | **0** |
20 | | Intervenções humanas | **0** |
21 | | Falhas de build | **0** |
22 | | Duração | 1787957770244 → 1787958336489 ≈ **9 min 26 s** |
23 | 
24 | Sequência: um turno de 6 chamadas em paralelo para investigar (`list_files`,
25 | `read_file` × 3, `update_todo_list`) → escreve o `Dockerfile` → `docker build` →
26 | `docker run` → `curl -X POST /api/todos` → `stop`. Reto, sem volta.
27 | 
28 | ## Decomposição da janela
29 | 
30 | | Origem | Tokens | % de 10.439 |
31 | |---|---:|---:|
32 | | `toolDefinitions` | 5403 | 51,8% |
33 | | `toolSystemPrompts` | 2470 | 23,7% |
34 | | `skills` | 1541 | 14,8% |
35 | | `staticSections` | 563 | 5,4% |
36 | | `baseRules` | 197 | 1,9% |
37 | | `customInstructions` | 160 | 1,5% |
38 | | `environment` | 71 | 0,7% |
39 | | `roleDefinition` | 34 | 0,3% |
40 | | **`projectRules`** | **0** | **0,0%** |
41 | | `mcpToolDefinitions` | 0 | 0,0% |
42 | 
43 | ---
44 | 
45 | ## Detectores da Fase 3 contra este log
46 | 
47 | | Detector | Achados | Evidência |
48 | |---|---|---|
49 | | Releitura redundante | **0** | Cada `path` aparece uma vez só |
50 | | Retry após falha | **0** | Nenhum `isError: true` no arquivo inteiro |
51 | | Intervenção humana | **0** | Uma única mensagem `role: user`, a primeira |
52 | | `projectRules` zerado | **1** | `breakdown.projectRules === 0` |
53 | 
54 | **Um de quatro detectores dispara.**
55 | 
56 | ---
57 | 
58 | ## O problema com este baseline
59 | 
60 | A hipótese do experimento era o atrito documentado pela IBM: `npm ci` falhando por
61 | falta de `package-lock.json`. **Esse atrito não existe neste repositório.** O
62 | `list_files` do primeiro turno mostra `package-lock.json` presente, e o Bob acertou
63 | o Dockerfile de primeira.
64 | 
65 | O baseline saiu **limpo**: zero erro, zero retry, zero intervenção. Não há
66 | desperdício de execução para o `AGENTS.md` remover.
67 | 
68 | Consequência direta: **na régua atual do `METRICS.md` — turnos, intervenções, falhas
69 | de build — a Rodada B não tem de onde melhorar.** O delta daria zero, ou ruído.
70 | 
71 | ## Desvio de protocolo
72 | 
73 | `approvalConfig.allowed_permissions` veio **`["read", "todo", "execute"]`**. A regra 4
74 | do [`METRICS.md`](../benchmark/METRICS.md) manda deixar **só `read`** ligado nas duas
75 | rodadas.
76 | 
77 | Não invalida o baseline sozinho — mas a Rodada B **precisa rodar com exatamente esta
78 | mesma configuração**, `["read","todo","execute"]`, e não com `["read"]`. Se a
79 | comparação mudar a permissão, muda mais de uma variável e o resultado não vale.
80 | O mais barato é atualizar a regra 4 do `METRICS.md` para refletir o que de fato
81 | rodou, em vez de tentar reproduzir o baseline.
82 | 
83 | Há também `taskCommandApprovals` com `docker build -t express-todo-api-modern .`
84 | aprovado na task, e um `durationMs` de **128 s** num `update_todo_list` (ferramenta
85 | instantânea) — tempo parado esperando aprovação humana. Isso é medível e some com
86 | auto-approve, mas é atrito de UI, não de configuração do agente.
87 | 
88 | ---
89 | 
90 | ## Onde ainda existe delta real
91 | 
92 | O baseline não desperdiça **execução**, mas desperdiça **contexto**. Isso é medível e
93 | é a tese original do projeto:
94 | 
95 | 1. **`toolDefinitions` = 5.403 tokens, 51,8% do overhead.** `availableTools[]` na
96 |    primeira mensagem `user` lista as ferramentas ligadas; `toolCalls[].name` lista as
97 |    usadas. A diferença é imposto pago em toda sessão. **Cruzar as duas listas é o
98 |    achado mais forte do log** e nenhum dos quatro detectores planejados o pega.
99 | 2. **`skills` = 1.541 tokens com `loadedSkills: []`.** 14,8% do overhead em Skill que
100 |    a sessão não declarou ter usado.
101 | 3. **`projectRules` = 0.** O achado central continua de pé.
102 | 
103 | Somados, 1 e 2 são **6.944 tokens, 66,5% do overhead fixo** — pagos em toda sessão,
104 | antes de o agente ler uma linha de código.
105 | 
106 | ## Recomendação
107 | 
108 | Três caminhos, do mais barato ao mais caro:

1 | # AGENTS.md — Hindsight
2 | 
3 | Context for AI coding assistants. Keep this file short and stable.
4 | 
5 | ---
6 | 
7 | ## What this project is
8 | 
9 | A **static web app** (plus a dev CLI) that analyses IBM Bob session exports,
10 | identifies context waste, generates corrected configuration — `AGENTS.md`, tools to
11 | disable, Skills, MCPs, subagents — and compares two experiment rounds (A/B).
12 | 
13 | Pipeline: `export JSON → Parser → Observe → Diagnose → Prescribe → Compare → UI`
14 | 
15 | Everything runs **in the browser**. No backend, no database, no network calls, no
16 | API key. A session export contains source code, absolute paths, and the commands the
17 | user ran — it must never leave the machine. This is a hard constraint, not a
18 | preference.
19 | 
20 | `ObserveReport` is the central contract: after F2, **no module reads the raw export**.
21 | 
22 | ---
23 | 
24 | ## Repository map
25 | 
26 | ```
27 | benchmark/          experiment protocol, task prompt, and both round exports
28 |   METRICS.md        what is measured and the rules that make the comparison valid
29 |   rodada-a.json     Round A — baseline (same as fixtures/sample-export.json)
30 |   rodada-b.json     Round B — with generated config
31 |   task.txt          exact benchmark prompt (character-for-character)
32 | bob_sessions/       required screenshots of Bob sessions (submission deliverable)
33 | docs/
34 |   architecture.md   component responsibilities, data flow, dependency rules
35 |   domain-model.md   all domain types with invariants (source of truth for types)
36 |   technology-stack.md  stack decisions, commands, and justifications
37 |   schema.md         Bob export JSON structure, field-by-field
38 |   analise-rodada-a.md  findings from the baseline run
39 |   ROADMAP.md        phases F0–F7, gates, and Bobcoin strategy
40 | fixtures/
41 |   sample-export.json  faithful copy of rodada-a.json — use for all dev/tests
42 | data/               curated catalogues — versioned data, not code
43 |   mcp-catalog.json    binary → MCP server (drives enable-mcp)
44 |   tool-catalog.json   tool → purpose → group (groups unused-tool findings)
45 | src/
46 |   domain/types.ts   TypeScript interfaces for all domain types
47 |   parser/           F2: validates and normalises the raw export → Session
48 |   observe/          F2: extracts metrics from Session → ObserveReport
49 |   diagnose/         F3: pure detectors (ObserveReport) → Finding[]
50 |   prescribe/        F4: generates config artifacts from Finding[] + catalogues
51 |   compare/          F5: diffs two ObserveReports → Comparison
52 |   ui/               F6: the React SPA — this is the product
53 |   cli.ts            F6: same core, terminal output — dev tool only
54 | ```
55 | 
56 | ---
57 | 
58 | ## Canonical commands
59 | 
60 | All commands run from the repository root.
61 | 
62 | ```bash
63 | npm ci                # install — use npm install only when adding a dependency
64 | npm test              # run tests (vitest run)
65 | npm run test:watch    # watch mode during development
66 | npm run typecheck     # tsc --noEmit — run before every commit
67 | npm run dev:web       # vite — the SPA with hot reload (this is the product)
68 | npm run build:web     # vite build → dist/web/ (static, deployable)
69 | npm run preview       # vite preview — check the static build locally
70 | npm run dev           # tsx src/cli.ts — CLI without building
71 | npm run build         # tsup → dist/cli.js
72 | npm run demo          # build + run the CLI over fixtures/sample-export.json
73 | ```
74 | 
75 | ---
76 | 
77 | ## Code and test conventions
78 | 
79 | - **TypeScript strict mode.** `strict: true` in tsconfig.json. No `any`.
80 | - **One module per pipeline stage.** `parser → observe → diagnose → prescribe → compare → cli`.
81 |   Dependencies flow downward only — see `docs/architecture.md` for the
82 |   full prohibition list.
83 | - **Test files alongside source.** Pattern: `src/**/*.test.ts` and `src/**/*.test.tsx`.
84 |   Fixtures go in `fixtures/`; tests import from there.
85 | - **Pure functions for detectors.** Each detector in `src/diagnose/` is
86 |   `(ObserveReport) => Finding[]` with no side effects.
87 | - **No rounding in domain.** `Math.round`, `toFixed`, and truncation are
88 |   forbidden in `src/domain/`, `src/parser/`, `src/observe/`, `src/diagnose/`,
89 |   `src/prescribe/`, and `src/compare/`. Round only in `src/cli.ts`.
90 | - **Timestamps are epoch milliseconds.** Type `EpochMs = number`. Never
91 |   convert to `Date` or ISO string before the presentation layer.
92 | - **Subtasks excluded from aggregation.** `task.parentId !== null` = subtask.
93 |   Never add its cost/tokens to session totals (invariant I-5).
94 | - **The core must stay browser-safe.** No Node APIs (`fs`, `path`, `process`, `os`)
95 |   anywhere except `src/cli.ts`. The web build imports the same modules.
96 | - **No network, ever.** No `fetch`, `XMLHttpRequest`, WebSocket, telemetry — in any
97 |   module, including the UI. The bundle is self-contained.
98 | - **No LLM calls.** Recommendations are rule + catalogue, deterministic and traceable
99 |   to a field in the export. Calling a model would break demo-without-API-key, static
100 |   deploy, privacy, and explainability at once. See `docs/architecture.md`.
101 | - **Never render export content as HTML.** No `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, `innerHTML`
102 |   or `eval`. The export is untrusted input in the browser too.
103 | - **Absence is not zero.** A metric the export does not provide goes into
104 |   `unavailableMetrics` or stays `null` — never `0`. Estimates must be labelled as
105 |   estimates (invariant I-6).
106 | 
107 | ---
108 | 
109 | ## Confirmed schema traps (read before touching parser or tests)
110 | 
111 | These bugs have been confirmed on the real export — do not re-discover them:
112 | 
113 | | Trap | Correct behaviour |
114 | |---|---|
115 | | `messages[].createdAt` is identical for all messages | Order by `data._meta.timestamp` |
116 | | `_meta.spend` only exists on `assistant` messages | Guard the access — accessing it on `tool` or `user` crashes |
117 | | One `assistant` turn can have N parallel `toolCalls[]` | Correlate by `.id`, never by position |
118 | | `task.status` stays `"active"` after completion | Use `stop: true` on the last assistant message |
119 | | `contextWindowBreakdown.total` ≠ `reportedTotal` | Intentional: `total` = fixed overhead, `reportedTotal` = overhead + conversation |
120 | | `gitSha` and `gitBranch` are always `null` | Record commit SHA manually via screenshot |
121 | | `tasks[].task.parentId !== null` = subtask | Do not double-count it in session aggregates |
122 | | `_meta.spend` is `undefined`, not `null`, when absent | Use optional chaining: `msg.data._meta.spend?.cost` |
123 | 
124 | ---
125 | 
126 | ## Policy: sensitive data
127 | 
128 | **Never print, log, or copy into a generated artefact:**
129 | - `data.content` of user or assistant messages
130 | - `toolCalls[].arguments` (may contain file paths, commands, or code)
131 | - `toolUsage.signature.arguments`
132 | - `task.title` (it is the full prompt, often verbatim code)
133 | - `task.env.staticEnvInfo.primaryWorkspace` (absolute path)
134 | 
135 | These fields are available internally for analysis but must be redacted
136 | (`[REDACTED]`) before any output visible to the user, unless the user
137 | explicitly enables raw display.
138 | 
139 | The `evidence.redactable` flag on a `Finding` marks which evidence fields
140 | need redaction. Check it before rendering.
141 | 
142 | Catalogues in `data/` are the exception: they are **trusted input** (versioned and
143 | reviewed in PR), so their text may be rendered directly.
144 | 
145 | ---
146 | 
147 | ## Where to implement each phase
148 | 
149 | | Phase | Files to create/modify | Input type | Output type |
150 | |---|---|---|---|
151 | | **F2 — Observe** | `src/parser/`, `src/observe/` | raw JSON bytes | `Session`, `ObserveReport` |
152 | | **F3 — Diagnose** | `src/diagnose/` | `ObserveReport` | `Finding[]` |
153 | | **F4 — Prescribe** | `src/prescribe/` | `Finding[]` | `Prescription[]`, `AGENTS.md` draft |
154 | | **F5 — Verify** | `src/compare/` | two `ObserveReport`s | `Comparison` |
155 | | **F6 — Interface** | `src/ui/` (product), `src/cli.ts` (dev) | all of the above | four screens / terminal output |
156 | 
157 | Each module has its own test file(s). The fixture for all tests is
158 | `fixtures/sample-export.json` (copy of the real Round A baseline).
159 | 
160 | ---
161 | 
162 | ## Definition of Done (per issue)
163 | 
164 | A task is done only when:
165 | - acceptance criteria are covered by a test or recorded evidence
166 | - `npm test` passes
167 | - `npm run typecheck` passes
168 | - invalid input fails with a readable message
169 | - no secret or private content appears in output
170 | - the result has been verified against `benchmark/rodada-a.json` when applicable
